actions.description: Check out a connected GitHub repository onto this project's machine so its files can be read and edited directly instead of one REST call at a time. Shallow; refresh by calling again with the same repo.

input_schema.description:
Arguments for a brokered read-only checkout onto the project machine.

Deliberately not idempotency-keyed: a checkout is a converge-to-a-ref
operation, so repeating it is the normal way to refresh and the receipt
already reports whether anything moved.

discard_local_changes.description: Only set this after the user has explicitly agreed to discard uncommitted changes in an existing checkout.

provider.description: Only needed when both GitHub and GitLab are connected and neither grant settles which host holds this path. Otherwise the Gateway resolves the host from the project's connections.

ref.description: Branch, tag, or full 40-character commit SHA. Omit for the repository's default branch.

repo.description: Repository as owner/name (GitHub) or group/subgroup/project (GitLab), e.g. acme/website.

actions.description: Freeze every edit made in a checked-out repository into one commit and return its SHA and the list of changed files. Nothing reaches GitHub; push the returned commit_sha to send it.

input_schema.description:
Arguments for freezing the checkout's current edits into one commit.

Naturally idempotent rather than idempotency-keyed: repeating the same
prepare finds a clean tree and returns the commit it already made, so a
retry after a lost response restates the freeze instead of creating an
empty second commit.

message.description: Commit message describing the change, in the user's terms.

provider.description: Only needed when both GitHub and GitLab are connected and neither grant settles which host holds this path. Otherwise the Gateway resolves the host from the project's connections.

repo.description: Repository as owner/name (GitHub) or group/subgroup/project (GitLab); it must already be checked out.

actions.description: Push one prepared commit to a new or previously pushed branch and verify the branch by reading it back. Never force-pushes, never touches the default branch; merging stays a separate approved step.

input_schema.description:
Arguments for pushing one prepared commit to a branch.

Naturally idempotent: a repeat that finds the branch already at
``commit_sha`` reports success rather than colliding with its own earlier
push.

branch.description: Branch to create or update. Never the default branch. An existing branch is only writable if this project's checkout created it.

expected_remote_sha.description: The commit the branch is expected to be at right now. Omit to create a branch that does not exist yet; the push is refused if the branch has moved since it was read.

provider.description: Only needed when both GitHub and GitLab are connected and neither grant settles which host holds this path. Otherwise the Gateway resolves the host from the project's connections.

repo.description: Repository as owner/name (GitHub) or group/subgroup/project (GitLab); it must already be checked out.

actions.description: Install a checked-out repository's dependencies from its lockfile (pnpm, npm, yarn, uv, or requirements.txt) so its tests and build can run. Answers 'installing' while the work continues; call again after poll_after_seconds until it reports installed.

input_schema.description:
Arguments for installing a checkout's dependencies from its lockfile.

Naturally idempotent: the same lockfile installs once and every later
call reports ``installed``; a call while an install runs reports
``installing`` with a poll interval rather than starting a second one.

provider.description: Only needed when both GitHub and GitLab are connected and neither grant settles which host holds this path. Otherwise the Gateway resolves the host from the project's connections.

repo.description: Repository as owner/name (GitHub) or group/subgroup/project (GitLab); it must already be checked out.

actions.description: Promote one validated sandbox artifact into cloud Library when active, or the shared workspace on legacy projects. The receipt distinguishes cloud saving from pending local materialization.

idempotency_key.description: Use one fresh key for each new logical operation. Reuse that key only when retrying the exact same arguments; a later user request, even with identical content, needs a new key.

staged_path.description: Path relative to the attempt directory; it must be under promote/ (the sandbox exposes this directory as MAGISTER_PROMOTION_DIR).
